outlook: Soybeans steadied overnight after Monday's selloff, when November beans closed 15¼ cents lower at $12.41¼ as Lula's surprise win in Brazil sent the Brazilian real to its steepest one-day drop since 1999; the real stabilized overnight. Corn and wheat stayed soft on a lack of fresh demand news: December corn closed Monday down 1 cent at $4.55 after bouncing off a 3½-month low, and Minneapolis spring wheat fell 7½ cents to $6.34 as Black Sea peace-talk hopes keep wheat near its lowest level since July. Monday's USDA Crop Progress put the U.S. corn harvest at 60% (vs. 66% average) and soybeans at 79% (2 points ahead of average), with winter wheat 76% planted. ICE canola was down about C$3.70 early Tuesday.
